First, the Gibson. From what I know, a Gibson cocktail is similar to a gin martini but with a pickled onion instead of an olive. So, it definitely has gin as a base ingredient. I've seen recipes that include gin, dry vermouth, and the onion. So, I'm pretty confident that the Gibson contains gin.

Now, the Zurracapote. I'm less sure about this one. I think it's a Spanish drink, maybe from La Rioja. From the conversation, I saw that the traditional recipe includes red wine, sugar, cinnamon, and lemons. There's also mention of dried fruits like apricots and raisins. I didn't see any gin in the ingredients listed by the sources, like the NYT Cooking recipe or Spain.info. So, the Zurracapote itself doesn't contain gin, but it might have a flavor similar to gin because of the berries.
